chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abd al-'Aziz, from Abu 'Azzah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by me while I was in the fifth lap of the circumambulation. He said to me, 'Go ahead so that we may return here as one person.' I said, 'I am in five laps of my seven; I will complete my seven.' He said, 'Cut it [the circumambulation short], and preserve the part you have completed from the place where you stop, until you return to the spot from which you cut off, and build upon it [to complete the count].'

key_terms.الشَّوْط: A single lap or circuit of the Tawaf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for completing Tawaf if one has to stop in the middle?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'Qat'' (interruption) in Tawaf is clarified, establishing that a pilgrim need not restart from the beginning if paused, but rather resume from the exact point of departure. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding ritual validity, emphasizing that the continuity of the act is maintained by marking the specific spot where the break occurred. It serves as a practical guideline for pilgrims to manage fatigue or distractions without invalidating their worship.
